newsitem.title: USA: Mobil says business changes necessary.
newsitem.headline: Mobil says business changes necessary.

text.p: Mobil Corp said it needs to change the way that it conducts its business in order to compete in the volatile energy industry.
The company reported third quarter operating income fell 10 percent from year-ago levels to $668 million.

"Since we are in a very competitive industry that has significant price volatility, changes in the way we run our business are essential if we are to compete in the long term. We are not counting on continuing high oil prices to enhance shareholder value," said chairman Lucio Noto in a statement.
Mobil did not specify the types of changes needed, saying only that it will pursue its strategy of improving the performance of existing businesses and providing growth.

The company attributed its disappointing results to unfavorable market conditions in many of its businesses, especially as strong crude prices hurt refining and marketing results. It also cited an unexpectedly high level of unscheduled refinery downtime in the U.S.
Other unfavorable factors included paraxylene pricing pressure and higher exploration expenses for overseas operations.

Mobil also said the company saved about $160 million before tax from restructuring programs. However, those savings were offset by higher volume-related expenses that included costs for new growth programs.

U.S. exploration and production income rose $106 million to $152 million in the third quarter, mainly due to higher crude and natural gas prices. International upstream income rose $14 miliion to $270 million.
Mobil said U.S. refining and marketing tumbled $65 million to $83 million due to weak margins. Unscheduled refinery downtime hurt earnings by $25 million, the company said.
International downstream income fell $81 million to $148 million. The company cited lower margins in Europe and the Asia-Pacific region.
Chemical income fell $89 million to $90 million in the third quarter.
